name: β-Oxidation
summary: Mitochondrial matrix during fasting. Fatty acids are activated to acyl-CoA in the cytosol, then long chains need the carnitine shuttle: CPT I (rate-limiting, inhibited by malonyl-CoA) and CPT II. Each round shortens the chain by 2 carbons and yields 1 FADH₂, 1 NADH and 1 acetyl-CoA; palmitate takes 7 rounds → 8 acetyl-CoA (≈106 ATP net). Defects (MCAD, CPT, carnitine) cause hypoketotic hypoglycemia with fasting. Odd chains end in propionyl-CoA → succinyl-CoA (B12-dependent).

fa.name: Fatty acid
fa.notes: From adipose lipolysis (hormone-sensitive lipase), carried on albumin.

acylcoa.name: Fatty acyl-CoA (cytosol)
acylcoa.notes: Can't cross the inner mitochondrial membrane on its own (short and medium chains can).

acylcarn.name: Acylcarnitine
acylcarn.notes: Crosses the inner membrane via carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase. Elevated acylcarnitines on newborn screening point to fatty acid oxidation defects.

shorter.name: Acyl-CoA (n−2)
shorter.notes: Re-enters the spiral at acyl-CoA dehydrogenase until the chain is used up.

acetylcoa.name: Acetyl-CoA
acetylcoa.notes: Goes to the TCA cycle, or to ketone bodies in the liver when OAA is scarce.

acs.name: Fatty acyl-CoA synthetase
acs.notes: ATP → AMP + PPi: costs 2 high-energy bonds per fatty acid.

cpt1.name: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase I
cpt1.notes: Rate-limiting; outer mitochondrial membrane. Inhibited by malonyl-CoA. Hepatic CPT I deficiency: hypoketotic hypoglycemia. Primary carnitine deficiency (OCTN2 transporter) blocks the shuttle too: weakness, hypotonia, cardiomyopathy, hypoketotic hypoglycemia.

cpt2.name: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase II
cpt2.notes: Inner mitochondrial membrane, matrix side. Adult CPT II deficiency (most common): exercise- or fasting-induced muscle pain and rhabdomyolysis with myoglobinuria.

acad.name: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase
acad.notes: FAD-linked; chain-length-specific isoforms (VLCAD, LCAD, MCAD, SCAD). MCAD deficiency (autosomal recessive, most common FAO defect): fasting hypoketotic hypoglycemia, vomiting, lethargy, seizures, sudden death; C8–C10 acylcarnitines and dicarboxylic aciduria. Treat by avoiding fasting.

ech.name: Enoyl-CoA hydratase
ech.notes: Adds water across the double bond.

hadh.name: 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase
hadh.notes: NAD⁺-linked. The long-chain form (LCHAD, part of the trifunctional protein) — fetal LCHAD deficiency is linked to maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy and HELLP.

thiolase.name: 3-Ketoacyl-CoA thiolase
thiolase.notes: CoA cleaves off acetyl-CoA, leaving an acyl-CoA two carbons shorter.

cact.name: Carnitine–acylcarnitine translocase
cact.notes: Inner-membrane antiporter: acylcarnitine in, free carnitine out. Long-chain fatty acids need the whole carnitine shuttle; short and medium chains enter the matrix directly.

tissue: muscle, heart, liver (not brain or RBCs)
